figure.name: Ayn Rand
figure.role: Writer and philosopher who popularized Objectivism, rational self-interest, individualism, property rights, and laissez-faire capitalism.
figure.hook: Rand = capitalism as moral individualism, not just market efficiency.
whyHere: Rand belongs here because she made capitalism a moral story for millions of readers, not just an economic model.
She matters because Objectivism turns private property, individual achievement, self-interest, and anti-collectivism into a full political philosophy.
figure.cleanIdea: Rand's capitalism argument says individual rights and productive self-interest are moral foundations, not embarrassments to apologize for.

ideas.title: Objectivism
ideas.plainDefinition: Objectivism is Ayn Rand's philosophy of reality, reason, self-interest, individual rights, and laissez-faire capitalism.
ideas.context: In the Rand path, capitalism is defended as the political system that protects individual achievement and property rights.
ideas.whyMatters: Objectivism matters because it is one of the most influential popular moral defenses of capitalism in U.S. political culture.

ideas.title: Laissez-Faire
ideas.plainDefinition: Laissez-faire is a view that economic life should be left largely to private exchange, property, contract, and competition with minimal state interference.
ideas.context: In the Rand path, laissez-faire becomes a moral demand for individual rights, not only an efficiency claim.
ideas.whyMatters: Laissez-faire matters because many capitalist arguments treat government intervention as the main danger to freedom.

sources.title: Objectivism / Wikipedia
sources.note: Source lead for Rand's laissez-faire capitalism claim.

ideas.title: Rational Self-Interest
ideas.plainDefinition: Rational self-interest is the idea that people should pursue their own life, values, achievement, and happiness through reason rather than sacrifice or coercion.
ideas.context: In the Rand path, self-interest is defended as moral when joined to reason, production, and voluntary exchange.
ideas.whyMatters: Rational self-interest matters because it is the moral doorway into Rand's defense of capitalism.
